A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified several candidate genes and genetic polymorphms that could be associated to the phenotypic differences existing between IB pigs and IBxDU crossbreds.

the transcriptome analysis of muscle tissue from IB and IBxDUs pigs allowed us to identify several candidate genes, transcription factors, pathways and polymorphisms that may be involved in meat quality and performance differences between these two pig genotypes.
we identified genes and regulatory mechanisms potentially involved in the phenotypic differences observed between purebred and Duroc crossbred Iberian pigs at early age.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the observed differences between IB and Duroc crossbred Iberian pigs in meat quality and productivity traits could be associated to differences in the regulation of genes involved in muscle and adipose development, lipid metabolism and protein catabolism.
the observed phenotypically differences between IB and IBDX pigs are associated to gene expression differences and to genetic variation.
